site.sitedescription: Tsuga candensis, Fagus grandifolia, Acer saccharum, Pinus strobus, and Betula species are common in the northern, inland, and higher-elevation parts of New England. Quercus, Carya, and Castanea dentata dominate in the warmer southern part of the region. Acer rubrum is common across New England. Pinus rigada is prevalent on sites with well-drained sandy soils.
